findings.title: Resource lookups filter on the wrong owner
findings.body: The three-argument `findByName` lookup filters by resource owner, but client resources are created with `resourceServer.getClientId()` as their owner, whereas this code passes `server.getId()`; the all-clients lookup at line 244 uses the same mismatch. As a result, per-client lookups miss their resources and the all-clients lookup misses its resource, so V2 client permissions are not recognized.

findings.title: Existing permission clients are not upgraded with the Clients schema
findings.body: Adding Clients to `SCHEMA` does not update realms that already have an admin-permissions client: `init` returns immediately when that client exists, without creating the new Clients resource or scopes. After upgrading, those realms cannot create or evaluate client permissions because the required schema entries are absent.

findings.title: Role-mapping checks drop the MANAGE_CLIENTS role
findings.body: These V2 overrides (and the composite and client-scope variants below) authorize only through the new scope permissions; they omit the existing `MANAGE_CLIENTS` role check that client-management operations retain in `canManage`. Consequently, administrators granted `MANAGE_CLIENTS` cannot map client roles or composites under V2 unless they also receive separate authorization policies.
